summary: Aries is Mars's own sign; 0-12° is its moolatrikona and 12-30° own sign. It gives courage, drive, truthfulness and leadership, with a fondness for adventure and competition, and some exposure to injury.
common_outcomes: Leadership in teams, groups or organisations
Love of adventure, sport and competition
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 18.5: wealth through army command or trade; wanders; acquires goods even through a thief
Saravali 25.1-2: village or group head; generous with cattle, goats and grain
Brihat Jataka 18.5: injuries to the body

by_area.personality: Splendid, truthful, brave, fierce and adventurous (Saravali 25.1-2); organising capacity, commanding, pioneering, frank and generous but combative (Raman HPA ch. XXII).
by_area.career: Army chief or head of a village or band (Saravali 25.1-2); wealth through command or trade (Brihat Jataka 18.5); Raman: statesmanly, mathematician.
by_area.finance: Brihat Jataka 18.5: gains through command or trade; Raman: rich but not economical in domestic dealings.
by_area.health: Brihat Jataka 18.5 mentions bodily wounds and Raman scars; frame as a need for safety in risky activity, not a prediction.
by_area.relationships: Saravali 25.1-2: joins many women; Raman: sensual.

Kendra from lagna or Moon forms Ruchaka yoga: daring, wealthy, victorious, an army leader (Phaladeepika 6.1-2, 6.4)
Kendra placement; Braha (p. 50) says planets in kendras are powerful and prominent

Jupiter's aspect (Saravali 25.25-30: learning, fortune, wealth, kingly results for Mars in its own signs)
Sun's aspect (Saravali 25.25-30: wealth and justice)
Exalted or own sign in the navamsa, or vargottama (Braha pp. 13-14, 59-60)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Venus's aspect (Saravali 25.25-30: loss and trouble through relationships)
Mercury's aspect (Saravali 25.25-30: deceit)
Saturn's aspect (Saravali 25.25-30: loss of followers)
Combustion (within about 8 degrees of the Sun), which Braha (pp. 17, 61) says spoils a planet
lagna_or_context_notes: Mars in Aries in a kendra forms Ruchaka yoga (Phaladeepika 6.1-2): Aries (1st), Capricorn (4th), Libra (7th), Cancer (10th) lagnas; Phaladeepika 6.4 also counts kendras from the Moon. Braha ('Planets in the Houses', pp. 79 ff.) reads the own-sign Mars house by house: Aries lagna (1st) success, respect, courage; Capricorn lagna (4th) land and houses, a strong but discordant bond with the mother; Libra lagna (7th) marriage still strained but a better-quality spouse; Cancer lagna (10th) a great career with wealth and fame; Gemini lagna (11th) ambitions realised. Braha (p. 67) counts Mars in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th as Kujadosha unless it is in that house's exception sign; with Mars in Aries this applies to Capricorn (4th), Libra (7th), Virgo (8th), Taurus (12th) lagnas, while Aries lagna (1st) is exempt. He notes some astrologers use the 2nd house instead of the 1st. For Cancer lagna Mars alone forms rajayoga as lord of the 5th and 10th (Braha p. 53).

Grateful and kind to children and friends

summary: Mars is debilitated in Cancer (deepest fall at 28°), though Cancer's lord, the Moon, is a friend. The fiery planet in a watery sign gives emotional reactivity, indirect assertion and unsettled living conditions, yet texts also give prosperity through water-related work; neecha bhanga is frequently present.
common_outcomes: Repeated distress and anguish (Saravali 25.7-8); bold and headlong (Raman HPA ch. XXII)
Unsettled home life or living in others' homes
Gains through agriculture, water or shipping
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 18.6: prosperous through water-borne trade, wise, possibly physically impaired
Saravali 25.7-8: enjoys royal food and robes in childhood; eats in others' homes

by_area.personality: Repeatedly anguished and distressed (Saravali 25.7-8); wise (Brihat Jataka 18.6); bold, dashing, speculative, fickle and egoistic (Raman HPA ch. XXII). Frawley (p. 126): with the debility cancelled it can give mastery over the feeling nature and a capacity for profound relationships.
by_area.career: Agriculture and water-borne trade (Brihat Jataka 18.6; Saravali 25.7-8); Raman: love of agriculture, medical and surgical proficiency, travels and voyages.
by_area.finance: Wealth through water or farming despite distress (Brihat Jataka 18.6; Saravali 25.7-8); Raman: wealthy.
by_area.health: Texts mention illness and bodily impairment (Saravali 25.7-8; Brihat Jataka 18.6) and Raman defective sight; never present as a prediction.
by_area.family: Lives and eats in others' houses (Saravali 25.7-8).

strengtheners: Neecha bhanga: Moon (sign lord) or Saturn (lord of Capricorn, Mars's exaltation sign) in a kendra from lagna or Moon (Phaladeepika 7.26, 7.29)

Saturn's aspect (Saravali 25.43-48: wealth through water journeys, king-like)

weakeners_or_cancellations: Near 28 degrees Cancer, the deepest fall (BPHS 3.49-50)
Moon's aspect without other support (Saravali 25.43-48: various diseases, unhappiness)
Mercury's aspect (Saravali 25.43-48: lowly conduct, rejected by own people)
Venus's aspect (Saravali 25.43-48: insult and loss through women)
Placement in a dusthana (6th, 8th, 12th); Braha (pp. 51-52) says a planet there is spoiled, the 6th being the mildest
Vargottama does not help a fallen planet; Braha (pp. 13, 59) says it leaves it worse off
lagna_or_context_notes: Braha ('Planets in the Houses', pp. 79 ff.) reads the fallen Mars harshly house by house: Cancer lagna (1st) health and self-respect suffer, though Mars as 5th and 10th lord still gives some benefits there; Aries lagna (4th) strain around home and mother; Capricorn lagna (7th) a difficult marriage; Libra lagna (10th) career difficulties and changes. Frawley (p. 126) instead says debility is much reduced in an angle, especially the 10th, so the 1st, 4th, 7th and 10th cases above are where the two authors pull in opposite directions. Braha (p. 67) counts Mars in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th as Kujadosha unless it is in that house's exception sign; with Mars in Cancer this applies to Cancer (1st), Aries (4th), Capricorn (7th), Leo (12th) lagnas, while Sagittarius lagna (8th) is exempt. He notes some astrologers use the 2nd house instead of the 1st. For Cancer lagna Mars alone forms rajayoga as lord of the 5th and 10th (Braha p. 53).

disagreements: Brihat Jataka calls the native prosperous and wise despite debility; Saravali stresses distress. phrasing_guidance: Do not call it a 'bad Mars'. Describe protective, emotional energy that works best when expressed openly; note that cancellation is common. No illness, disability or marriage-failure predictions.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (1986), 'Mars' p. 23, 'House Rulerships' pp. 50-53, 'Shad Bala' pp. 59-61 and 'Kujadosha' p. 67
source_views.view: Mars does well in the upachaya houses and best in the 10th (directional strength); kendras are powerful, trikonas flourish, dusthanas spoil; combustion within about 8 degrees spoils a planet; dignity in the navamsa strengthens; Mars in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th gives Kujadosha unless in the exception sign; for Cancer lagna Mars alone forms rajayoga.

disagreements: Both texts are negative; Saravali also contains a harsh death-related line that this library deliberately omits. Aspect verses show Jupiter or Saturn aspect as strongly redeeming. Braha says Mars is well placed in Aquarius as the other sign of Saturn, whose Capricorn is its exaltation, which runs against both classical verses and Raman.
phrasing_guidance: Present as independent energy that can feel blocked; suggest steady, structured effort and caution with risk-taking. Never mention manner of death, addiction or moral labels.
